title: The last one renting discs
lede: Redbox was one of the things that finished off [the video store](/blockbuster/). It then outlasted every other way of renting a disc, including the one that had seemed to be the future.

blocks.title: Four ways to rent a disc. None is left.
blocks.subtitle: The businesses Redbox competed with or absorbed, and what became of each.

items.name: Redbox
items.text: At the end of 2013. Shut down on the conversion to Chapter 7 in July 2024.[^11][^26]

items.name: Blockbuster
items.text: At the end of 2004.[^36] Redbox had more points of sale than that by the end of 2008, with 13,700 kiosks.[^6]

items.name: NCR’s DVD kiosks
items.text: Paid by Redbox in June 2012 for about 6,200 active kiosks, which it replaced or removed.[^10][^11]

items.name: DVDXpress
items.text: A smaller kiosk operator. Coinstar had lent it $4.5M by 2006 and acquired it in October 2007.[^3][^5]

items.name: Netflix DVD by mail
items.text: DVD revenue in its last year, down from $182.3M in 2021. The same company’s streaming revenue was $33.6 billion.[^35]

blocks.source: Company filings as cited. Sparklines: Redbox year-end kiosks for 2008–2013, 2015, 2021 and 2023[^6][^8][^9][^11][^13][^17][^22]; Netflix DVD revenue 2021–2023[^35].
